entry.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
entry.summary:
We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #distributed-systems #agents

entry.title: A Unifying Metatheorem on Weak-Memory Robustness
entry.summary:
Memory models specify the behaviors that concurrent programs may exhibit under compiler and hardware optimizations, which often deviate from Sequential Consistency (SC). Robustness is the property of a program P not exhibiting any weak behaviors when executing under a weak memory model MM, compared to SC. As such, the algorithmic problem of deciding whether $P$ is robust against MM has been studied extensively, and has been repeatedly shown to be in PSPACE for many memory models, such as TSO, PSO, and Release/Acquire.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #logic

entry.title: Python Code Generation for Isabelle/HOL. The Isabelle theorem prover provides an environment for formalising mathematics and reasoning about programs.
entry.summary:
The Isabelle theorem prover provides an environment for formalising mathematics and reasoning about programs. To make verified implementations practically usable, its code generator translates functions expressed in the executable fragment of its logic into conventional programming languages. Its targets have traditionally been functional languages (Standard ML, OCaml, Haskell, and Scala), recently joined by Go.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #logic #software-architecture

entry.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
entry.summary:
Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #ml-theory #distributed-systems
